ns2:course.label: Empirical Methods in Applied Economics
ns2:course.description: Covers techniques in modern applied econometrics, with an emphasis on reduced-form causal inference. These methods form an important foundation for engagement with much of the literature in agricultural and applied economics. The course surveys research designs, with an emphasis on their identifying assumptions for causal inference. To prepare for future research, students will use software with data to apply these methods in problem sets. Prerequisite: ECON 502 or equivalent.
